latin.418: §. IV. Cæterùm à Causa non causa oriundæ Transsubstantiationis ad VERAM ORTUS EJUS CAUSAM deveniendum est, in Idololatria & Tyrannide, Papismi vera anima huicque summum Antichristianismi dedecus conciliaturis, locatam.
latin.419: Enimvero accidit, ut exactis Seculis Ecclesiæ Catholicæ Apostolicis, verè Episcopalibus atque Patristicis, saltem fine hisce cunctis imminente, Seculo admodum sexto imaginum sacrarum usus cultusque in templis invalescere inciperet, superioribus temporibus non tantùm inauditus prorsus, sed etiam ex omnium Protestantium Confess. publica majorem in modum exosus.
latin.420: Hinc facilè inventi sunt qui novæ idolomaniæ sese opponerent in Constantinop. IV. Concilio, vulgò dicto Oecumenico septimo, sub Leone Isauro & Constant. Copronymo, celebrato, decreto Patrum 380. unanimiter facto, imagines nullas, minimè omnium Dei Christique figuras in templis tolerandas esse.
latin.421: Subnexâ ratione disertissimâ, quòd veræ Christianæ Ecclesiæ de nulla alia Christi Figura, quicquam unquam innotuisset, præterquam ea, quæ in S. Eucharistia detur, inque Pane consecrato conspicua sit. Sic enim Conciliorum Epitomator Sagittarius Constantinopolitanorum mentem ac Constitutionem edisserit.
latin.422: Quòd dixerint: Quænam est hæc insana opinio pictorum, ut lucri turpis & miseri causa ea quæ efficere nequeunt, studeant conficere, ut & ea quæ ore & corde sunt tantummodo confessa, impiis manibus figurare intendant? Damnati autem à cordatis viris in eo quòd incomprehensibilem & incircumscriptibilem Divinam Christi naturam ipsi depingere studuerunt, ad aliam aliquam pravâ inventione apologiam confugiunt, quòd solius carnis, quam vidimus & palpavimus & cum qua versati sumus, illius, inquam, imaginem exhibeant: quod sane impium est & Nestoriana Diabolica inventio.
latin.423: Et paucis intersertis: Exultent & lætentur & libertate linguæ fruantur, quicunque veram Christi imaginem sincerissimâ mente facientes desiderant & venerantur & ad salutem animæ corporisque adferunt, quam ipse Dominus noster Deus summus sacerdos, ex nobis integrè massam assumens, circa passionis tempus, in typum & recordationem efficacissimam, suis sacerdotibus & mystis tradidit: nam cum se sponte morti objiceret, gloriosa inquam illi & vivificanti, sumens panem benedixit, postquam gratias egisset & fregit tradensque discipulis dixit: accipite, manducate: Hoc est corpus meum. Ecce igitur vivificantis corporis illius imaginem quæ honorificè & gloriosè exhibita est. Quia quemadmodum id quòd è nobis assumsit, materia sola est substantia humana, juxta omnia non perfectè expressa, quæ per se existit persona, ne adjectio in Divinitate accidat; ita & imaginem totam electam, videlicet panis substantiam, mandavit apponi, ne scil. humanâ effigie figurata induceretur idololatria. Similiter etiam panem Eucharistæ veluti imaginem veram naturalis carnis per Sancti Spiritus aggressionem sanctificatam, divinum corpus esse voluit, illique sic placuit &c. &c. Lege ipsum Sagittarium p. m. 354. 355. & seq.

pass_a.418: §. IV. But from the non-cause of Transsubstantiation’s origin one must come down to the TRUE CAUSE OF ITS ORTUS, located in Idolatry and Tyranny — the true soul of Papism and things about to win for it the highest disgrace of Antichristianism.
pass_a.419: For it happened that when the Apostolic, truly Episcopal and Patristic centuries of the Catholic Church were finished — or at least with the end of them all imminent — about the sixth century the use and cult of sacred images began to grow strong in temples, in earlier times not only utterly unheard-of, but even from the public Confession of all Protestants hated in a greater degree.
pass_a.420: Hence easily were found those who would oppose themselves to the new idolomania in the Fourth Constantinopolitan Council, commonly called the Seventh Oecumenical, celebrated under Leo the Isaurian and Constantine Copronymus, by a decree of 380 Fathers unanimously made, that no images at all, least of all figures of God and of Christ, were to be tolerated in temples.
pass_a.421: With a most express reason annexed: that to the true Christian Church nothing had ever become known concerning any other Figure of Christ except that which is given in the Sacred Eucharist and is conspicuous in the consecrated Bread. For so Sagittarius, Epitomator of the Councils, sets forth the mind and Constitution of the Constantinopolitans.
pass_a.422: That they said: What is this insane opinion of painters, that for the sake of base and wretched gain they strive to fashion what they cannot effect, and intend with impious hands to figure even those things confessed only by mouth and heart? But condemned by stout-hearted men in that they themselves strove to paint Christ’s incomprehensible and uncircumscribable Divine nature, they flee by a wicked invention to another apology — that they exhibit an image of the flesh alone, which we saw and handled and with which we lived: which is indeed impious and a Nestorian Diabolic invention.
pass_a.423: And with a few things inserted: Let them exult and rejoice and enjoy freedom of tongue, whoever with sincerest mind desire and venerate and bring to the salvation of soul and body the true image of Christ, which our Lord God Himself, the high priest, taking an entire mass from us, around the time of the passion handed to His priests and initiates as a type and most efficacious remembrance: for when He was casting Himself spontaneously to death — that glorious and life-giving [death] — taking bread He blessed, after He had given thanks, and broke and giving to the disciples said: take, eat: This is My body. Behold therefore the image of that life-giving body which was honorably and gloriously exhibited. Because just as that which He assumed from us is matter alone, human substance, not perfectly expressed according to all things by which the person exists through itself, lest addition happen in the Divinity; so also He commanded the whole chosen image to be set forth — namely the substance of bread — lest idolatry be induced by a human effigy figured. Likewise also He willed the bread of the Eucharist, as a true image of natural flesh sanctified by the approach of the Holy Spirit, to be a divine body, and so it pleased Him &c. Read Sagittarius himself, pp. 354–355 and following.

418: §.IV: leave the non-cause; the TRUE CAUSE of Transsubstantiation’s Ortus sits in Idolatry and Tyranny.
That pair is Papism’s true soul, and will win it Antichristianism’s highest disgrace.
419: When the Apostolic / Episcopal / Patristic centuries were spent (or nearly ended), about the sixth century sacred-image use and cult began to strengthen in temples.
Earlier ages had never heard of it; Protestant public Confessions hate it still more.
420: Opponents of the new idolomania gathered in Constantinopolitanum IV (popularly ‘Seventh Oecumenical’) under Leo the Isaurian and Constantine Copronymus.
380 Fathers unanimously: tolerate no temple images — least of all figures of God and of Christ.
421: Annexed reason, most express: the true Church never knew any other Figure of Christ than the one given in the Sacred Eucharist and seen in the consecrated Bread.
Sagittarius (council epitomator) reports the Constantinopolitans’ mind and constitution so.
422: Sagittarius’s quote: what insane painters’ opinion — for base gain they try to figure with impious hands what mouth and heart alone confess?
Condemned for painting Christ’s incomprehensible, uncircumscribable Divine nature, they invent a flesh-only image apology — impious, and a Nestorian diabolic invention.
423: The true image of Christ they honor is what the High Priest Himself handed at the passion as type and efficacious remembrance: blessed, broken bread — ‘This is My body’.

As the assumed humanity is material substance (lest Divinity get an addition), so He commanded bread’s substance as the whole chosen image — lest a human effigy breed idolatry; Eucharist bread, Spirit-sanctified true image of natural flesh, He willed a divine body (Sagittarius pp. 354–355).
